static_traits.name: Lin Wanqing
static_traits.educational_background: Currently studying for a bachelor's degree
static_traits.social_status: Growing distant from friends and classmates due to anxiety, reduced socializing; having one close friend's support but not yet fully asking for help
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment before; no similar academic problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic; able to self-reflect; highly cooperative, positive attitude; steady speech rate; able to describe physical anxiety symptoms concretely

basic_info.main_problem: High-intensity stress and anxiety from failing some courses, starting at the beginning of the self-study period and worsening month by month; worrying about being expelled from school and unable to get a degree; anxiety especially strong when receiving homework or exam grades, affecting sleep and diet.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling when anxiety started affecting my daily functioning and overall well-being.
growth_experiences: Once failed a math exam in high school, thinking it irreversible at the time, but through continuous effort and adjusting learning methods, finally achieved good grades at the end of the term; this experience shows resilience and ability to recover from setbacks.

core_beliefs: My future will be ruined by failure

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my grades are not ideal this time, I will keep failing and be expelled, ending up without a degree
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling study efforts, seeking tutoring, constantly doing practice problems to try to control the outcome
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be expelled and never get a degree

special_situations.event: Nearing exams or entering exam week
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get high scores on the next exam, it proves I'm no good and I will keep failing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Making a high-pressure study plan, trying to make up for unease with intensive review
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not do well this time, I will fail at everything in the future

special_situations.event: Thinks of the tuition debt one carries and current academic performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot graduate smoothly and find work, these debts will ruin my life, all my efforts are in vain
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repressing emotions, putting all energy into studying to avoid 'failure'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These debts are all wasted, my future is over

special_situations.event: Considers sharing difficulties with close friends or seeking support
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I ask for help, I will become a burden on others and be resented
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Choosing not to reveal true difficulties, isolating oneself to avoid causing others dissatisfaction

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be understood and supported, to be recognized as a capable student and graduate smoothly
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being expelled after failure, disappointing family, being judged as useless
defense_goal: Reducing loss of control and failure through strengthened self-control and high-pressure studying
Keeping distance and not asking for help to avoid becoming a burden on others and being negated

object_relations.self_representation: Easily seeing oneself as a student who may fail and trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: Family / others are experienced as potential judges or people easily disappointed

object_relations.self_representation: A person who must keep working hard to barely maintain worth
object_relations.object_representation: Others are experienced as examiners of one's value and sources of recognition

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests sharing true difficulties with family and friends or seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously interprets 'seeking help' as becoming a burden and being disliked by the other party (transference: others will be disappointed / judge)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing in a tactful and restrained tone 'I should not trouble others', displacing the topic to self-solutions with objective reasons (they are busy, etc.), reducing emotional exposure.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to examine the evidence for catastrophic predictions and discuss the realistic probability of failure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Transforms emotional worries into rational analysis to maintain distance from emotions (transference: worrying others underestimate the problem)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a rational, analytical tone, emphasizing probabilities and plan details, downplaying subjective feelings, reducing the use of emotional vocabulary.

manifestations: Growing distant from friends and classmates due to anxiety
Unwilling to ask close friends for help out of worry about being a burden
Worrying tuition debts will be wasted, efforts may be meaningless
Seeing one or a few failures as the negation of the entire career
outcomes: Rising sense of helplessness and despair

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly using self-rules like 'I should not trouble others' and 'I must do well on exams'
Internalizing 'must not fail' as an absolute demand

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Has the urge to seek help but isolates instead
Bearing pressure and anxiety inward, exerting control over oneself with high-pressure studying

exception_events.target_problem: In exam or grade-receiving situations, the client usually makes catastrophic predictions with strong anxiety, disrupting sleep and diet, decreasing learning efficiency.
exception_events.unique_outcome: After failing a high school math exam, the client worried at the time about being 'unable to recover', but kept adjusting study strategies in the following semester, gradually improving, and finally achieved good grades at the end of the term — different from the stagnation after past catastrophizing, showing recovery and progress.
exception_events.reason: Clues: despite initial failure, the client maintained study investment and strategy adjustments, and gave herself time; this led to an outcome different from the catastrophic anticipation in that situation.

positive_force: Having resilience to recover from setbacks (having turned failure around in high school)
Having actively sought tutoring and planned learning
Willing to face problems and seek professional help
Having a caring and supportive close friend
negative_force: Cognitive tendencies toward catastrophizing and overgeneralization
Overly dependent on external recognition, worries about disappointing family
Social withdrawal and self-isolation, reduced support obtained
Anxiety affecting sleep and diet, further weakening learning and resilience

target_behavior.behavior: High anxiety in exam and grade-related situations (with palpitations, sense of breathing difficulty)
antecedent: Nearing exam week or taking exams
Thinking about possibly being expelled and not getting a degree
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic beliefs about failure consequences and negative predictions about the future, amplified by tuition-debt pressure
target_behavior.function: Avoiding and reducing perceived threats, temporarily relieving unease through control and high-pressure studying
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired sleep and diet, decreased learning efficiency, overall functioning affected

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance and self-isolation (avoiding asking friends and classmates for help)
antecedent: Situations requiring sharing difficulties with others or seeking support
When advised to communicate with family and friends
Thinking about 'being a trouble to others'
target_behavior.core_reason: The introjected rule of 'must not trouble others / should not fail' and worrying about being judged or disappointing others
target_behavior.function: Avoids possible negative evaluation and shame, maintaining superficial self-control and safety
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, worsened loneliness, anxiety persisting and repeatedly intensifying
